Within-host pN/pS ratio

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/selection.R
pNpSWithinHost.Rd

Computes, for each sample, the ratio of nonsynonymous to synonymous polymorphism per site among its iSNVs. This is a within-host polymorphism ratio, pN/pS: it counts variants segregating inside one host, not substitutions fixed between two sequences, so it is not the dN/dS of a between-sequence comparison and carries no multiple-hit correction. Sites are counted with the method of Nei and Gojobori (1986). For dN/dS between hosts or between consensus sequences, use the models in the MSA2dist package.

Usage

pNpSWithinHost(x, cds, ref, ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,TxDb,DNAStringSet'
pNpSWithinHost(x, cds, ref, usePassedOnly = TRUE, ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,GRangesList,DNAStringSet'
pNpSWithinHost(x, cds, ref, usePassedOnly = TRUE, geneCol = NULL, ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,GRanges,DNAStringSet'
pNpSWithinHost(
  x,
  cds,
  ref,
  usePassedOnly = TRUE,
  txCol = "ID",
  geneCol = "gene",
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,ANY,character'
pNpSWithinHost(x, cds, ref, ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,ANY,XString'
pNpSWithinHost(x, cds, ref, ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment,character,DNAStringSet'
pNpSWithinHost(x, cds, ref, ...)

Arguments

x

A WithinHostExperiment with ref and alt columns in mcols(rowRanges(x)).

cds

The coding sequences, as for annotateCodonChange: a TxDb, a GRanges of CDS records, or a GRangesList with one element per transcript.

ref

A DNAStringSet with the reference sequence of each seqlevel carrying coding sequences, for example from Biostrings::readDNAStringSet().

...

Not used; supplying anything is an error.

usePassedOnly

Logical. If TRUE (default), only iSNVs with qcPass == TRUE are counted.

txCol, geneCol

As for annotateCodonChange: the transcript and gene columns of a GRanges or GRangesList cds.

Value

A DataFrame with one row per sample and gene carrying at least one counted iSNV (one row with gene = NA when a sample has none):

sample_id

Sample identifier.

nS, nN

Synonymous and nonsynonymous iSNVs in the sample.

S_sites, N_sites

Synonymous and nonsynonymous sites over all coding sequences.

pS, pN

The proportions \(n_S/S\) and \(n_N/N\).

pNpS

\(p_N/p_S\); NA when \(n_S = 0\).

gene, gene_nS, gene_nN, gene_S_sites, gene_N_sites, gene_pNpS

The same quantities for each gene.

Details

With \(n_S\) synonymous and \(n_N\) nonsynonymous iSNVs present in a sample, and \(S\) synonymous and \(N\) nonsynonymous sites in the coding sequences, $$p_S = n_S / S, \quad p_N = n_N / N, \quad \mathrm{pN/pS} = p_N / p_S.$$ Under the assumptions of the counting model (every substitution equally likely, no selection) the expected ratio is 1. A ratio below 1 is what purifying selection against amino acid changes would give, but a within-host ratio rests on few iSNVs, is highly variable, and should always be read with its counts. It is NA when no synonymous iSNV is present.

Classification. The counts use only the codons and the genetic code that the sites are counted over. This function calls annotateCodonChange on x with the same cds and ref, so annotation columns already present in x are not used, and takes from it, for each transcript reading an iSNV, the reference and variant codon. A reading counts only when its reference codon is a sense codon: an iSNV in a stop codon, including the loss of a stop codon, is counted in neither \(n_S\) nor \(n_N\), since a stop codon carries no sites. The reading is then classified by translating both codons with the standard genetic code: synonymous when the amino acid is kept, counting towards \(n_S\), and nonsynonymous otherwise, a change to a stop codon included, counting towards \(n_N\). The initiator rule is not applied, so ATG to CTG or TTG at the first base of a coding sequence is nonsynonymous here, as ATG carries no synonymous site, although annotateCodonChange reports it as synonymous.

The totals take each iSNV by its first counted reading, in the order of collapse = "longest": the longest transcript that reads it in a sense codon, and where that transcript reads the nucleotide twice, the first of those readings in a sense codon. Each gene's counts take it by the first counted reading of that gene's own transcripts, so an iSNV in a codon two genes share counts in both genes, as the codon's sites do, but once in the total. Sites outside every coding sequence, insertions and deletions, and codons holding an ambiguous base are not counted. An iSNV is present in a sample when its frequency is above zero and, with usePassedOnly = TRUE, it passed QC; it is counted once whatever its frequency.

Sites. \(S\) and \(N\) are summed over the distinct codons of the genome that some coding sequence reads: a codon is identified by the genomic positions of its three bases, so where two coding sequences read the same bases in the same frame (ORF1a inside ORF1ab in SARS-CoV-2) the shared codons are counted once, while coding sequences that overlap in different frames (ORF7a and ORF7b) contribute their codons separately. Each sense codon carries three sites, split between synonymous and nonsynonymous under the standard genetic code; stop codons and codons with an ambiguous base carry none, so \(S + N\) is three times the number of distinct sense codons. When coding sequences of different transcripts overlap, a warning names them with the nucleotides and codons they share. The sites of a gene are summed in the same way over the codons of that gene's own transcripts, so a codon shared by two genes is counted in each of them but once in the total.

Relation to MSA2dist. MSA2dist::codonmat2pnps() and MSA2dist::dnastring2kaks() compare pairs of aligned sequences codon by codon, so they cannot take a set of per-site iSNV calls, each present in a sample at its own frequency; that is why the sites are counted here. Codon for codon the counts agree: each of the 61 sense codons carries the same Nei-Gojobori synonymous and nonsynonymous sites here as in MSA2dist::codonmat2pnps(). They differ only at stop codons, which carry no sites here but a third or two thirds of a synonymous site there, so over a coding sequence holding stop codons the two totals differ.

References

Nei M, Gojobori T (1986). Simple methods for estimating the numbers of synonymous and nonsynonymous nucleotide substitutions. Mol Biol Evol 3:418-426. doi:10.1093/oxfordjournals.molbev.a040410

See also

annotateCodonChange for the reference and variant codons of each iSNV, from which the classification here is made.

Examples

## A 15-nucleotide coding sequence, ATG CTG AAA GGG TAA
ref <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(c(seg1 = "ATGCTGAAAGGGTAA"))
cds <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("seg1", IRanges::IRanges(1, 15),
    strand = "+", ID = "cds-A", gene = "geneA")
## 1 A>G is ATG -> GTG (nonsynonymous); 6 G>A is CTG -> CTA (synonymous)
gr <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("seg1",
    IRanges::IRanges(c(1, 6), width = 1))
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$ref <- c("A", "G")
S4Vectors::mcols(gr)$alt <- c("G", "A")
whe <- WithinHostExperiment(
    assays = list(altFreq = matrix(c(0.1, 0.2), ncol = 1)),
    rowRanges = gr,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_id = "S1"))
if (requireNamespace("txdbmaker", quietly = TRUE)) {
    pNpSWithinHost(whe, cds, ref)
}
#> DataFrame with 1 row and 14 columns
#>     sample_id        nS        nN   S_sites   N_sites        pS        pN
#>   <character> <integer> <integer> <numeric> <numeric> <numeric> <numeric>
#> 1          S1         1         1   2.66667   9.33333     0.375  0.107143
#>        pNpS        gene   gene_nS   gene_nN gene_S_sites gene_N_sites gene_pNpS
#>   <numeric> <character> <integer> <integer>    <numeric>    <numeric> <numeric>
#> 1  0.285714       geneA         1         1      2.66667      9.33333  0.285714
